newsitem.title: CYPRUS: SOCCER-CYPRUS NATIONAL TEAM COACH QUITS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CYPRUS NATIONAL TEAM COACH QUITS.

text.p: Cyprus's national soccer coach Andreas Michaelides has resigned, local sporting officials said on Friday.
Michaelides's resignation came hard on the heels of claims that Cyprus's World Cup qualifier against Bulgaria in December was rigged and in the midst of an official inquiry into the allegations.
Michaelides, the coach since October 1991, cited personal reasons for his resignation in a letter sent to the Cyprus Football Association on Thursday.
There was a public furore earlier this month over widespread rumours of match-rigging. Cyprus lost 3-1 to Bulgaria in Limassol.

"He is in a difficult position," said a member of the Football Association. "There are international matches next month and he would have faced the dilemma of who to call up because then suspicion might fall on those he would leave out."

A three-man commission appointed by the Cyprus Sports Association (KOA) has been questioning players and officials in closed-door meetings throughout the week. Michaelides was one of the first to testify.
The commission has to report its findings to KOA in a month's time.
Cyprus are due to play in a friendly tournament against Poland, Lithuania and Latvia in mid-February, while at the end of March they have another World Cup qualifier, against Russia.
